title: The Key Closest to a Target

concept.title: Walk down like a search and remember the best value seen
body: Find the value in the tree that is closest to a target number. Walk down from the root as if you were searching for the target: at each node compare the node with the best value found so far, and then go to the side where the target would be. Values in the other subtree are farther away than this node, so they cannot be closer than the nodes you will still meet on the road.

body.code:
def closest(root, target):
    best = root.val
    cur = root
    while cur is not None:
        d, bd = abs(cur.val - target), abs(best - target)
        if d < bd or (d == bd and cur.val < best):    # a tie goes to the smaller value
            best = cur.val
        if target == cur.val:
            break
        cur = cur.left if target < cur.val else cur.right
    return best

body: When two values are equally far from the target (one smaller, one larger), the problem asks for the **smaller** one, so the comparison needs the extra tie rule. The walk uses only the path from the root, so it takes O(h) time.

statement: Given a binary search tree and an integer `target`, print the value in the tree that is closest to the target. If two values are equally close, print the smaller one.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.
The tree is a binary search tree (all values are different).

examples.note: The value 3 is in the tree: distance 0.
The closest value to 6 is 5, at distance 1.

hints: Walk from the root as if you looked for the target.
At every node update the best value if the node is closer (or equally close and smaller).
Go left when the target is smaller than the node, otherwise right.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
